## 5. Distribution obligations and unresolved decisions

The primary text is [GPLv3](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html), preserved locally as `ostc4_baseline/COPYING.html`. The following is an engineering assessment of §§1–7 and 10–12; legal review of the concrete release arrangement remains open.

- Private modification/use does not itself trigger source publication. Conveying source or object code to others triggers the relevant conditions; a public repository containing only the extracted engine does not satisfy obligations for a distributed combined firmware.
- For the covered combined work, provide the preferred form for modification, local modifications, interfaces and scripts controlling compilation and installation. Include board/devicetree/configuration, CMake, generator/patch inputs, required non-exempt linked dependency source, dependency revisions and practical rebuild instructions. Assess System Library exclusions under §1 individually; an embedded SDK label is insufficient.
- Select an actual §6 delivery method. For network binary downloads, §6(d) permits equivalent access to Corresponding Source with clear directions and no further charge. For devices conveyed physically, determine the appropriate §6(a) accompaniment or §6(b) written offer and its duration/support requirements. A casual promise or moving branch URL is insufficient. Preserve exact release source with matching binaries.
- Under §5 license the covered whole under GPLv3-compatible terms, preserve component notices and identify changes/dates. Retain applicable Apache/BSD/SEGGER notices in the distribution materials and source. Do not add a no-modification/no-reverse-engineering EULA to GPL rights. Check applicable interactive-interface notice requirements before a real watch UI release.
- A consumer dive watch is likely a §6 User Product. Determine whether possession/use is transferred in the covered transaction and whether anyone retains the ability to install modified object code. When applicable, supply Installation Information: documented flashing/update procedure, necessary authorization information/keys and formats sufficient to install and execute a modified covered version. Warranty/support for modified software is not required by that clause. Record a reasoned exception only if its actual conditions hold; do not assume unsigned development linking proves compliance.
- Bootloader/secure-boot/DFU design, protection/debug unlock policy, actual installation path, release signing and rights to redistribute dependency sources are **not established**. Current ELF has no complete installable update package. These are release blockers, not a demand to publish unrelated secrets.
- The mobile companion and hardware design are not automatically GPL-covered merely by communicating with the watch. Reassess if code is copied or combined. No message was sent to a manufacturer or third party during this investigation.

[Apache's compatibility statement](https://apache.org/licenses/GPL-compatibility.html) supports inclusion of Apache-2.0 components in GPLv3 work. [The GNU licensing FAQ](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html) explains corresponding-source and library issues; [the runtime exception](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gcc-exception-3.1.html) applies only where its terms actually cover the runtime. Direct GNU license-page requests timed out in this session; the preserved primary text and installed exception were inspected rather than falsely claiming fresh HTTP retrieval. The local Nordic license is decisive evidence for the banner concern.
